claude_only.name: Which identifier is the authoritative master-system identifier for this contract, and which system of record issues it?
Does the contract carry a governed global identifier or IRI in addition to its local identifier, and is that IRI resolvable?
Which specification and dialect does this artefact declare itself to be written in, and is that declaration machine-readable?
Is a content fingerprint computed for the schema, and over which canonical form is it computed?
Which specific datasets, topics, tables or message types does this contract govern, and by what binding mechanism?
At what granularity does one contract instance apply - one object, one product, one domain or one tenant?
Does the contract govern the entire target or only a declared subset of its fields and partitions?
What happens when two contracts claim authority over the same target?
Which versioning scheme governs this contract, and what rule decides when the major component increments?
Once published, is the version immutable, and what mechanism prevents in-place edits?
Which version precedes and which supersedes this one, and how is that chain expressed to consumers?
How many versions may be simultaneously in force, and how does a consumer pin to one?
What is the closed set of permitted status values, and is it drawn from a controlled vocabulary?
Which status transitions are permitted, and which are forbidden or require a waiver?
At what instant does a status change take effect, and is that instant recorded separately from when it was observed?
Which statuses make the contract binding on producers, and which make it advisory only?
Which single party is accountable for the correctness of this contract, and how is that party identified?
Who is authorised to approve a breaking change, and is that authority delegable?
What is the fallback when the named owner is absent, has left, or the role is vacant?
Which agent is recorded as having authored each version, distinct from who approved it?
What is the full set of objects and properties, including nesting depth and array element definitions?
Is the structure closed, or may an instance carry properties not declared in the contract?
Does property ordering carry meaning for the physical representation, and where is that ordering authoritative?
Which property definitions are reused from a shared definitions library rather than declared locally?
Which uniqueness constraints hold beyond the primary key, and over what scope are they evaluated?
Which declared relationships point at other datasets, and is referential integrity enforced or merely asserted?
What is the agreed behaviour when a referenced target row is missing or arrives late?
What logical type is declared for each property, and from which type vocabulary is it drawn?
What physical type and physical name does each property take in each target platform?
For numeric and decimal properties, what precision, scale and rounding behaviour is guaranteed?
How is absence distinguished from an explicit null and from a defined sentinel value?
How are date and time values represented, and does the representation carry an explicit offset?
Which timestamp property carries event time and which carries observation or ingestion time?
What character encoding, collation and normalisation form apply to text properties?
For quantity properties, what unit of measure is guaranteed and is it stated in the contract or assumed?
Where is the authoritative definition of each business-significant property held, and is it dereferenceable?
Which properties draw values from an enumerated value domain or code list, and which list version applies?
Is the concept registered in a metadata registry as an administered item, and what is its registration status?
Where does the contract's local meaning of a property deliberately diverge from the governed definition?
What value constraints apply to each property, expressed in which constraint vocabulary?
For each declared constraint, is it an enforced assertion, an annotation, or documentation only?
Which properties are mandatory, and does mandatory mean present, non-null, or both?
Which declared formats are actually validated by the deployed toolchain, and which are advisory?
Which constraints apply conditionally, and on what condition are they triggered?
Which constraints require reading a second dataset, and who is responsible for executing them?
In which language or engine is each non-structural constraint expressed, and is that expression portable?
At what point in the data flow is each constraint evaluated - on write, on publish, or after the fact?
What type is each quality rule, and is it executable as written or only human-readable?
What metric, comparison operator, threshold value and unit define pass or fail for each rule?
What severity and business impact attach to a failure, and does failure block publication?
On what schedule is each rule evaluated, and against which slice of the data?
Which quality dimension does each rule serve, and is the dimension vocabulary controlled?
In what output format are validation results produced, and does it identify the failing instance location?
What exactly does a conformance result assert, and against which contract version was it evaluated?
How long are validation reports retained, and what triggers their deletion?
Which timestamps are recorded for a validation run, distinguishing the data's event time from the run's observation time?
Which compatibility mode is in force for this contract, and is it set globally or per subject?
Given the mode, which party must be upgraded first when a new version is published?
What test determines that a proposed change is breaking, and is that test automated?
Is compatibility checked only against the immediately previous version or against all prior versions?
Which properties carry default values, and what do those defaults mean when a writer omits the field?
How are renames handled - through aliases, through stable column identifiers, or not at all?
Which type changes are treated as safe widening, and which force a new major version?
Are partitioning and sort order versioned independently of the schema, and who tracks that?
What events may trigger a contract change, and which of them are producer-initiated versus consumer-requested?
Which registered consumers are affected by the proposed change, and how was that determined?
Who approved the change, on what date and offset, and on what evidence?
What minimum notice period must elapse between approval and the change taking effect?
What distinguishes a deprecated version from a retired one in terms of what the producer still guarantees?
At what instant does support for this version end, and is that instant published in advance?
What migration path is offered to consumers, and who bears the migration cost?
What happens to data already produced under a retired version - is it re-written, re-interpreted or left as-is?
Which party produces the data under this contract, and is there more than one producer?
Which consumers are registered against this contract, and how is registration recorded?
What role does each party hold, and what does that role entitle them to?
How is unregistered or shadow consumption detected, and what is the policy toward it?
What exactly does the producer commit to deliver, and in what form is that commitment testable?
What restrictions bind the consumer's use, redistribution and derivation of the data?
How does a consumer accept the contract, and over what period is that acceptance effective?
What counts as breach by either party, and what remedy follows?
Which service levels are promised - availability, freshness, latency, completeness of delivery, retention?
How is each service level measured, at which point, and by whom?
At what frequency is data updated, and what is the finest temporal resolution the data supports?
Through which channel is an issue raised, and what response commitment attaches to it?
What confidentiality classification applies to each property, and from which controlled vocabulary is it drawn?
Which properties carry personal or specially protected data, and on what basis was that determination made?
What protective measures does the contract require for classified properties - encryption, masking, tokenisation or pseudonym columns?
What retention period and deletion obligation does the contract state for the described data?
Are there jurisdictional or residency restrictions on where the described data may be stored or processed?
Which servers or environments does this contract bind to, and what distinguishes them?
In what serialization format and media type is the data made available for each binding?
How is the data partitioned or ordered physically, and is that part of the contract or an implementation detail?
Was this contract authored from a specification, inferred from data, or derived from another contract?
Which agent generated this version, and was that agent human, automated or a combination?
What inputs were used to produce this version, and are they retained for reproducibility?
When was this version generated, and when was that generation recorded in the registry?
In which registries or catalogues is this contract published, and which of them is the system of record?
Under what subject or record name is the contract published, and which naming strategy produced it?
How does a prospective consumer discover this contract and determine its applicability?
How is divergence between the registry copy and the catalogue copy detected and resolved?
In which schema languages is this contract expressed, and which expression is normative?
Which contract facts are lost or weakened when projected into each target language?
What evidence supports any claim that this contract conforms to a named standard?
Where do two aligned standards make contradictory requirements, and which one wins?
Which jurisdictional or sectoral profiles apply to this contract, and on what legal or policy basis?
Which profile-mandated properties and controlled vocabularies must the contract populate?
Do profile obligations differ between the publishing party and the receiving party, and how?
How is profile conformance demonstrated and re-verified after a contract change?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier does the governing catalog, schema registry or contract registry assign to this schema or contract?
What governed global identifier or IRI canonically identifies the schema resource, shape or named type regardless of file path?
What human-readable name, namespace and aliases distinguish this contract or named type from others in the same domain?
If no master-system identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and is a calendar date being misused as identity?
Is this artefact a DataContract, a JSON Schema document, a SHACL shapes graph, an Avro schema, or an OpenAPI Schema Object, and which kind value is declared?
Which meta-schema, apiVersion or dialect URI must a processor load before interpreting keywords?
Which vocabularies are required versus optional, and must a processor refuse the schema if an unknown required vocabulary is declared?
If a companion JSON Schema disagrees with the ODCS or OpenAPI standard text, which source is authoritative?
What is the current version of this data contract or schema, and how does it differ from the language standard version?
What is the current lifecycle status, and which transitions to deprecated, retired, deactivated or end of life are authorised?
Is deprecation or deactivation scoped to the whole contract, a shape, or a single property, and what replacement should consumers use?
When did this contract become generally available, and when are end of support and end of life scheduled?
What intended purpose, recommended usage and explicit limitations apply to consumers of this contract?
Which tenant, domain, data product owner or data steward is accountable for this contract?
Which authoritative definition URLs supply business meaning, licence, privacy terms or implementation mapping?
Who authored or registered this definition, and when was the definition event versus when was it ingested?
Which properties belong to each object, in what order, and which nested object or array items do they contain?
What is the declared data granularity of each object, such as grain of aggregation or uniqueness of a row?
Which refactor-safe element identifiers should be used in references instead of names that may change?
What logical type, format, pattern and bounds apply to each property, and is format an annotation or an assertion?
How does the logical type map to a physical datatype, Avro primitive or logical type, and are timezone or precision declared?
What enumerated symbols, const values or described permissible values constitute the value domain?
If the property represents time or location, which calendar, offset, geometry encoding or coordinate reference is required?
What business name, data-element concept, object class and property meaning does this element represent independently of its datatype?
What classification, tags and critical-data-element flag apply, and which code list authorises those values?
If values are encrypted at rest or in motion, what is the encrypted element name and how does it relate to the plaintext property?
Does this element carry personal or otherwise restricted data such that access, masking or purpose limitation in the contract must be enforced?
Which properties are required or unique, what are min and max counts, and is the shape closed against extra properties?
Which numeric bounds, string patterns, enums and formats must instance values satisfy?
Which constraints are warnings rather than violations, and which exceptions or ignored properties are authorised?
Which reusable definitions exist, and which $ref, named-type or shape IRIs must be resolved before evaluation?
How are subschemas combined (allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, union), and does adding a constraint follow open-world JSON Schema rules or Avro field lists?
Which nodes does each SHACL shape target, and what property path is constrained from the focus node?
What happens if a reference cannot be dereferenced, or if $dynamicRef depends on evaluation-time dynamic scope?
Which quality rules are bound to each object or property, of what type, metric and dimension, and what operator threshold must hold?
In what unit is the metric expressed, and is the comparison in rows, percent or another unit?
When is each quality rule scheduled to run, and what severity and business impact apply on failure?
What evidence artefact proves a quality rule passed or failed for a given evaluation event?
Which SLA properties are promised, on which elements, with what values, units and drivers?
What latency, frequency and time of availability apply, and under which scheduler?
What retention period is contracted, when does deletion or end of life occur, and which regulatory driver requires it?
Which SLA misses are authorised exceptions, and what time-to-detect, notify and repair apply when a miss occurs?
Which roles may access data under this contract, with what access mode, and who approves grants?
Which properties are readOnly or writeOnly, and what does the owning authority do if a consumer sends or requests them incorrectly?
What is the default access rule when no role matches, and which break-glass exceptions exist?
What decision record authorises a new consumer role binding to this contract?
What is the writer schema and the reader schema, and do they match under Avro resolution or JSON Schema constraint strengthening?
Which compatibility policy applies (backward, forward, full, or transitive variants), and which field additions or deletions are allowed?
Which reader fields have defaults, which names have aliases, and would a missing default signal an incompatible change?
When a compatibility check fails, what event is recorded and what exception process may override the block?
What instance, schema or shapes graph, dialect and engine are inputs to a validation run?
Did the instance conform, and which results with severity, path and value were produced?
When did the validation event occur, and when was the report ingested, if those times differ?
Which annotations (title, default, format) were collected from successful schemas, and are they used as evidence or only as hints?
What canonical form is used to decide whether two schemas are the same for reading, and which attributes are stripped?
What fingerprint algorithm and digest identify this canonical schema, and is it used as a cache key rather than as a security signature?
Which external standards is this contract aligned to, and which semantic conflicts are recorded instead of claimed conformance?
If string-encoded content declares contentEncoding or contentMediaType, is automatic decode disabled by default as JSON Schema requires for safety?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
